description: HRB's Type-III shape: A adds a component to compute() (r = r * 10) while B adds a transitive call on compute() (compute(5)). The merge would execute A's new component in a calling context that exists in B but not in A, printing 60 - a value neither contributor computes (A prints 30, B prints 3 and 6). We do not implement Type III (a documented scope limitation), but Type I rejects this instance anyway: B's new call site pulls compute()'s body into its changed-behaviour slice, so `return r` gains an in-edge from A's new component that B did not have. Measured, not assumed - and one instance is not a proof of subsumption.
category: Type-III shape caught by Type I (we do not implement Type III)
